title: Cost bound for a procedure call
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let $	ext{lim}$ be execution limits, and let $d,p,x,T,T'$ be natural numbers. Suppose there is a procedure body for $p$ whose execution at depth $d+1$, starting with local variables initialized from the argument values $	ext{vals}$ and memory $�mu$, has cost at most $T'$ and ends in a state with return value $r$ and memory $�mu'$ satisfying $R(r,�mu')$. Assume every pair $(r,�mu')$ satisfying $R$ gives a state with local variable $x$ set to $r$ and memory $�mu'$ that satisfies $Q$; the call arguments are safe in the initial state and evaluate to $	ext{vals}$; $d<\text{lim.depth}$; and their total expression cost plus $2+T'$ is at most $T$. Then calling $p$ with those arguments from the initial state has an execution of cost at most $T$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$.
